text: I can explain why random UUIDv4 primary keys degrade B-tree inserts as a table grows, and how UUIDv7's layout fixes it.
I can list what breaks when an auto-increment key meets sharding, offline clients or public URLs.
I can size a ticket server's range allocation for a given ID rate and state what each block size costs.
I can design a 64-bit Snowflake layout for given fleet size, throughput and lifetime, showing the arithmetic.
I can walk through a clock moving backwards under Snowflake and choose a defence (wait, refuse, max(now, last), slewing NTP).
I can pick between sortable and random IDs for a given storage engine and privacy requirement.
